[[Australian Army officer rank insignia#Company Grade Officer ranks|LT]] ([[Acting rank|T]]/[[Australian Army officer rank insignia#Company Grade Officer ranks|CAPT]]) Dr '''Edwin Harry Medlin''' (2 January 1920 – 6 March 2013)<ref>https://australiansatwarfilmarchive.unsw.edu.au/archive/htmlTranscript/1503?asPdf=y</ref> was [[List of University of Adelaide people#Deputy Chancellors|Deputy Chancellor]] of the [[University of Adelaide]] from 1978 to 1997.<ref name="obit">{{cite web |url=https://www.adelaide.edu.au/lumen/issues/63001/news63067.html |title=Harry Medlin, a remarkable man, a remarkable life |publisher=University of Adelaide |last=Husband |first=Kate |accessdate=16 May 2015}}</ref><ref>[http://www.blueandgoldalumni.com.au/nl/nl1305.pdf Obituary] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517102930/http://www.blueandgoldalumni.com.au/nl/nl1305.pdf |date=17 May 2017 }}, pg 3, May 2013 Newsletter, Adelaide Technical High School Old Scholars Association Inc.</ref>

==Early life and education==
Medlin was born in [[Orroroo, South Australia|Orroroo]] on 2 January 1920. His younger brother was the philosopher and activist [[Brian Herbert Medlin|Brian Medlin]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kovak|first=Anna|date=2015|title=ASIO's surveillance of Brian Medlin|url=https://dspace.flinders.edu.au/xmlui/handle/2328/36607|journal=Flinders Journal of History and Politics|volume=31|pages=112–138|id={{ProQuest|<!-- insert ProQuest data here -->}} }}</ref> He was sent to school in Adelaide, then studied at the [[South Australian School of Mines and Industries]] from 1936 to 1939. He worked for the [[Adelaide Electric Supply Company]] and enlisted in the [[Australian Army]] prior to Australia joining the [[Second World War]]. He was commissioned in 1939 and promoted to Captain in 1940. He was serving in the [[Sparrow Force|2/1st Fortress Company]] on the island of [[Timor]]<ref name="AWM">{{cite web |url=https://www.awm.gov.au/collection/S02918/ |title=S02918 |publisher=[[Australian War Memorial]] |date=9 December 1982 |accessdate=16 May 2015}}</ref> when he was captured by the Japanese and held as a [[prisoner of war]] in Timor from 23 February 1942 and transferred to [[Batavia, Dutch East Indies|Batavia]] in [[Java]] in September 1942<ref name="AWM"/> until he was freed on 23 September 1945. He was awarded the [[Efficiency Medal]] and five campaign stars and medals before leaving the army in 1946.<ref name="obit"/> He returned to Adelaide on a troop train from Melbourne on 28 October 1945.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article93337837 |title=More Men Home  |newspaper=[[The Chronicle (Adelaide)|The Chronicle]] |location=Adelaide, SA |date=1 November 1945 |accessdate=17 May 2015 |page=28 |publisher=National Library of Australia}}</ref> He had returned to Australia on the Hospital ship ''Manunda'' after being recovered from the POW camp on 18 September and started the journey home via Singapore on 23 September 1945.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://smartsheep.org/dr-harry-medlin-an-academic-physicist-has-lived-alone-in-craft-index-28 |title=2/AIF Service Record of SX 13860 Lieut. E.H. Medlin. |publisher=smartsheep.org |access-date=17 May 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518100403/http://smartsheep.org/dr-harry-medlin-an-academic-physicist-has-lived-alone-in-craft-index-28 |archive-date=18 May 2015 }}</ref>

Medlin studied under the [[Commonwealth Reconstruction Training Scheme]]{{citation needed|date=September 2018}} at the [[University of Adelaide]], graduating with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1949, Honours in 1951 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] on [[X-ray crystallography]] in 1956.{{citation needed|date=September 2018}}

==Career and research==
Medlin began lecturing at the university in 1951, rising to Associate Professor by 1974. He retired in 1985, but remained in the University environment, including becoming inaugural chair of the Alumni Association. He was a member of the University Senate Standing Committee from 1965 to 1980, and the University Council from 1967 to 2003. He was Deputy Chancellor of the University from 1978 to 1997.<ref name="obit"/>

Medlin was awarded the degree of [[Doctor of the University]] in 1987, and the [[Centenary Medal]] in 2001 "For creative and productive involvement in all aspects of the work, life and culture of universities".<ref name=CM>{{cite web |url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1115930 |title= Centenary Medal |date= 1 January 2001 |work=It's an Honour |accessdate=16 May 2015}}</ref>

Medlin's interests included membership and administrative roles in the University of Adelaide Staff Association, the Federation of Australian University Staff Associations, the [[University of Adelaide Theatre Guild]], the University of Adelaide Postgraduate Students Association (APSA) and the [[Adelaide University Union]].<ref name="obit"/>
